what_it_is: Mantis Skills: a portable toolkit of security-review skills for coding agents, published by Google under Apache-2.0. 33 markdown skills organised as a sequential pipeline (threat-model, plan, researcher, dedupe, review, critic, calibrate, report, and others).
use: FETCHED AND RUN ONLY. Nothing from that repository is copied into this one - not a skill, not a rule, not a sentence. This directory records what was run and what it produced; the toolkit itself stayed in a scratch directory outside the work tree.

how_it_was_run.targets: the same two file sets the treatment and control arms received
how_it_was_run.instruction: read their skills and follow their method as written; do not substitute another checklist
how_it_was_run.orchestrator: none - their pipeline expects one, so the single agent performed each stage itself, which is a deviation and is stated in the README
how_it_was_run.output: their own report, plus a neutral transcription of it so a third party can score it

stages_their_method_has_that_this_run_co: mantis-reproduce - their pipeline reproduces a finding by executing code. The targets here are file subsets with no build, and both of the other arms were static too, so the constraint is equal across arms; but their method loses a stage it has, and ours does not lose one it has.
